paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in Amos 7. When Amos saw the locusts, he didn't sit back and watch. He said, "Lord GOD, please forgive!" (Amos 7:2). Then the fire came, and he spoke up again: "Lord GOD, please stop!" (Amos 7:5). Twice he stood in the gap, and twice "the LORD relented from this plan" (Amos 7:3, 6). So go ahead and bring your worries to the Lord, because the passage shows He hears a prayer.

Now look at the third vision, because it's quieter and it's different. This time Amos doesn't ask for anything. The Lord stands by a wall true to plumb with a plumb line in His hand, and He says, "I will no longer spare them" (Amos 7:8). A plumb line shows what is straight, and I think that's the point: the Lord's standard doesn't bend to fit us. It also means the Lord's patience with Israel was real, and it still wasn't a license to keep going the wrong way.

So what do I do with that, baker? I hold both. I pray like Amos, boldly and often, and I keep measuring my life against what God says, not against what feels fine to me. My ovens stay ready, and I'd rather find out where I'm leaning now than later. The Lord isn't hiding the plumb line from you. He's showing it to you, same as He showed Amos, so you can get straight while there's still time.
